record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: Are any of the Borel splitting properties Split(BΩ, BΛ), Split(BΩ, BΩ), Split(BT, BT), or Split(BT, BΓ) hereditary?

evidence.quote: Are any of the properties Split(BΩ, BΛ), Split(BΩ, BΩ), Split(BT, BT), and Split(BT, BΓ) hereditary?

artifact.status_search_result: The splittability framework of Scheepers and Tsaban (Annals of Pure and Applied Logic, 2004) explicitly leaves heredity questions for several Split(U,V) properties open. Surveys on selection principles note that some Borel-case classes are provably hereditary, but available sources do not record a resolution of heredity specifically for Split(BΩ,BΛ), Split(BΩ,BΩ), Split(BT,BT), or Split(BT,BΓ). No subsequent paper located in the search confirms a solution.

status_evidence.title: The combinatorics of splittability
status_evidence.snippet: We consider the questions whether, given U and V, the property Split(U,V) is preserved under taking finite unions, arbitrary subsets, powers or products. Several interesting problems remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Heredity-type questions for Split(U,V) are left open in this foundational reference.

status_evidence.title: Some New Directions in Infinite-combinatorial Topology
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discusses hereditary nature of classes defined by selection principles for Borel covers.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys on selection principles discuss heredity but do not record resolution of these four cases.
